identity_basis: The official contact page names John S. and James L. Knight Foundation and lists Miami, Florida.
The official website identifies the organization as Knight Foundation.

facts.fact: Knight Foundation invests in local journalism, arts and culture, and community development in 26 cities and towns where the Knight brothers published newspapers.
In 2023, Knight announced a $150 million commitment through Press Forward to support local news over five years.
Its arts program prioritizes strengthening cultural ecosystems rather than standalone projects.
Its economic mobility strategy supports entrepreneurs and projects that expand local economic opportunity.

interests.label: Civic Engagement & Local News
interests.evidence: In 2023, Knight announced a $150 million commitment, as part of Press Forward.

interests.label: Arts & Culture
interests.evidence: We prioritize investments that strengthen a city’s broader cultural ecosystem rather than standalone projects.

interests.label: Community Development
interests.evidence: The foundation invests in local journalism, arts and culture and community development

interests.label: Economic Mobility
interests.evidence: Expanding local economic opportunity by supporting entrepreneurs

John S. and James L. Knight Foundation.notes: The donor is an institutional grantmaker, not an individual. Contact details are organization-level; employer and title are not applicable.

identity_basis: Exact foundation name matches its official website and Florida corporate registry.
Documented partnership with The Miami Foundation confirms its Miami-area philanthropic activity.
Registered location is Pompano Beach, Florida, rather than Miami; EIN is 65-0755554.

facts.fact: The foundation prioritizes economic mobility, youth and families, and responsive funding for nonprofit capacity building and Florida crisis relief.
A 2023 grant to Boys & Girls Clubs of America supported nine South Florida Clubs through academic programming, staff training, fundraising support and improved data systems.
The foundation lists Elisabeth DeLuca as president and Jonathan DeLuca and Suzanne Greco as directors.
Young Musicians Unite recognizes the foundation in its $500,000–$999,999 supporter tier.

interests.label: Arts & Culture
interests.evidence: Young Musicians Unite lists The Frederick A. DeLuca Foundation under its $500,000–$999,999 supporter tier.

interests.label: Community Development
interests.evidence: The 2023 BGCA grant funded staff training in program implementation and fundraising, alongside improved data efficiency.

interests.label: Education
interests.evidence: BGCA reports a 2023 foundation grant supporting nine South Florida Clubs, including academic success programming to reduce learning loss.

interests.label: Youth & Family
interests.evidence: A 2023 grant supported nine South Florida Boys & Girls Clubs and strengthened their capacity to serve youth.

interests.label: Food & Basic Needs
interests.evidence: Responding to emerging community needs including nonprofit capacity building and Florida- based crisis relief efforts.

interests.label: Economic Mobility
interests.evidence: Providing educational and professional pathways for individuals to support themselves and their families.

Frederick A. DeLuca Foundation.notes: Organization-level record. Miami is a documented service area, not the registered city. The website also represents the separate Elisabeth C. DeLuca Foundation; interests here use evidence explicitly tied to the Frederick A. DeLuca Foundation. No reliably verified public professional email or telephone was found.

identity_basis: Exact organization name appears on the firm's official website.
Official Miami office page confirms the city supplied.
The Miami Foundation identifies the firm as a local pro bono partner.

facts.fact: The firm's pro bono leadership includes Jayme Cassidy, Pro Bono Transactions Counsel based in Miami.
Lawyers for Good Government recognized the firm with its 2026 Pro Bono Award after its lawyers contributed more than 1,200 hours supporting the organization in 2025.

interests.label: Equity & Civil Rights
interests.evidence: The firm states: "We represent individuals seeking safety, freedom, and fairness." Its pro bono program expands access to justice for people unable to secure representation.

McDermott Will & Schulte.notes: Organizational donor, not an individual. The public email belongs to Miami office administrator Beatriz Soriano; it is not a designated philanthropy inbox. Documented Miami support is in-kind legal service, not a confirmed cash gift. Firmwide legal-aid evidence is distinguished from the local partnership.

identity_basis: Corporate donor name Amazon matches The Miami Foundation's announcement.
Documented grants to Miami-Dade and South Dade nonprofits match the supplied geography.

facts.fact: In January 2021, Amazon announced $500,000 for United Way organizations serving Miami-Dade and Broward counties during the pandemic.

interests.label: Food & Basic Needs
interests.evidence: Amazon's $500,000 United Way donation supported pandemic relief; the announcement describes utility assistance and support for local food banks.

Amazon.notes: Researched Amazon as a corporate donor, not Jeff Bezos or his separate philanthropic entities. Miami is treated as the giving geography, not a verified headquarters location. No direct public philanthropy email or phone was verified.
